newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ sees New Zealand unemployment rate rising.
newsitem.headline: BNZ sees New Zealand unemployment rate rising.

text.p: Companies "getting stuck into restructuring" could suppress economic growth in the short term but make it more sustainable in the long term, the Bank of New Zealand said in its July Economic Review published on Thursday.
The bank said companies with a renewed focus on increasing productivity would shed employees they had been "hoarding" since 1995.

"This labour shedding process is likely to boost the unemployment rate above 7.5 percent late this year or early in 1998, keeping consumer confidence low and further suppressing household spending level," BNZ said. The unemployment rate was
The BNZ said it welcomed this "mini round of restructuring" by companies because when the economy eventually picked up again in the first half of 1998 growth would be more sustainable.
The BNZ said companies should now cut costs they could have cut two to three years ago.
"Our advice to New Zealand business is if you haven't yet thrown your hands in the air and given up waiting on the Government to do something' its time to grow up and do so."
The most obvious way for companies to boost productivity was to reduce payrolls.
Overall the BNZ said it was less optimistic than the consensus about the timing of the economic recovery which many expect in the second half of this year.
Corporate restructuring was one factor which would suppress the timing of the upturn but it would also put exporters in a better competitive position.

The BNZ forecasts a trade-weighted currency index between 63.8 and 65.3 over the next three years against 64.89 this morning and 90-day bank bills between 7.3 percent and 8.5 percent against 8.21 percent this morning.
